new_in_this_version: M13 ops desk + recovery · the 72-hour clock in section F · queue inside Postgres, no Redis · files on disk, no MinIO · contracts D9 health and D10 ops API · run 4
how_to_use: This JSON is the full content of the drawing. Build from it.
Order: build_order.step_0 first (it includes the M13 safety net), then the three tracks in parallel, then join.
clock_72h gives the hour budget and the exit check for every block. recovery holds the no-data-loss targets.
decisions_closed are settled. Do not reopen them.
A module is done only when every item in its done_when list passes.
Contracts D1-D5 are frozen as zod schemas in packages/core before module work starts.
Items in needs.from_client are inputs to request from the lead. Do not invent them.
The default stack may be changed by the lead only if every contract and interface below is kept.
goal: Any website's articles become editable newspaper pages, go to InDesign as IDML for final polish, and the final PDF becomes a tappable e-paper. Many papers, any language, new sites plug in by configuration.

default_stack.storage: write-once files on local disk named by content hash; optional S3 driver (no MinIO)
default_stack.backups: WAL-G (Postgres) + restic (files) to an S3 bucket off the box
default_stack.ops: apps/ops: a standalone ops desk service
default_stack.ai: Claude API, model id from env
default_stack.deploy: Docker Compose + Caddy on one Linux box

rules.title: ONE ARTICLE SHAPE
rules.text: Every source is mapped into the canonical Article (D1). Nothing downstream knows or cares where it came from.

rules.title: ONE RENDERER
rules.text: A page is HTML + CSS drawn by Chromium, in the editor and on the server. Same package, same pixels.

rules.title: ONE SNAPSHOT
rules.text: All geometry leaves as the Layout Snapshot (D4): frames in mm, made by the one renderer. No exporter reads the editor's live DOM.

rules.title: TWO TRUTHS
rules.text: Browser = content truth. InDesign PDF = print truth. E-paper is built from the final PDF whenever one exists.

rules.title: AI SUGGESTS
rules.text: The editor decides. Nothing is applied without a tap. No new facts. The language never changes.

rules.title: PAPER_ID EVERYWHERE
rules.text: Many papers from the first migration: every row, every file key, every job carries paper_id.

rules.title: SAFE TO RE-RUN
rules.text: Everything slow is a queue job with an idempotency key. Running it twice changes nothing.

rules.title: FIXABLE BY THE OWNER
rules.text: Every service has a light, a restart, its logs and a way back on the ops desk (M13). State lives in two places only, both copied off the box.

decisions_closed: Postgres is the only database. The job queue lives inside it (pg-boss). No Redis
Files on local disk, named by content hash, written once. S3 driver optional. No MinIO
Backups: WAL-G for Postgres and restic for files, to an S3 bucket off the box
State lives only in Postgres and the files folder
One renderer: HTML + CSS in Chromium, for the editor and the server
InDesign hand-off is IDML. No InDesign Server
E-paper is built from the final PDF whenever one exists
The ops desk is its own service and never depends on the API, the worker or Postgres

state_lives_in: the files folder: named by content hash, written once
recovery.postgres: archive_timeout 60 s; WAL-G wal-push to the off-box bucket; base backup nightly; 30 days kept; point-in-time restore into a second Postgres, compare row counts, then switch; the old one kept 7 days
recovery.files: restic snapshot to the off-box bucket every 15 min; soft delete for 30 days; restore one file, one edition or everything
recovery.config: .env, ops/services.yml and the release list ride in the same encrypted snapshot
recovery.releases: tagged image sets, last 5 kept; expand-only migrations, so any of them runs on today's database
recovery.editor: unsaved typing is kept in the browser (IndexedDB) and saved when the API returns

targets.dead_disk_database: at most about 1 minute of writes

honest_limits: The ops desk lives on the same box. If the box is dead, run scripts/restore.sh on a new one
Zero loss on a dead disk needs a second server with a synchronous replica
The desk fixes services, queues, releases and data. A logic bug present in every kept release still needs a code fix
recovery.tool_note: WAL-G and restic are the default tools. The targets are the contract: swap a tool only if every M13 drill still passes.

modules.name: PLATFORM CORE
modules.purpose: The floor every module stands on.
modules.tech: TypeScript monorepo (pnpm) · Fastify + zod → OpenAPI · Postgres + Prisma · pg-boss job queue inside Postgres · files on disk or any S3 bucket · Docker Compose · Caddy
build: Repo (D7): apps/{api, worker, ops, editor, admin, reader} · packages/{core, connectors, assets, ai, layout, idml, export, epaper}
packages/core: zod schemas for Article, PageDoc, LayoutSnapshot, Zones — the only place types are defined
Auth: email + password (argon2), session cookie; roles owner · editor · sub · designer · viewer per paper; API key per source
Queues on pg-boss, inside Postgres: ingest · assets · ai · layout · export · epaper — retries with backoff, job log, dead-letter list
Files: {paper}/{yyyy-mm-dd}/{kind}/{hash}.{ext}, written once and never overwritten; drivers fs (default) and s3; signed URLs for anything private
State lives in exactly two places: Postgres and the files folder. Every container can be deleted and rebuilt from its image
Migrations are expand-only: add, never rename or drop in the same release, so any of the last 5 releases runs on today's database
Audit row on every write; soft delete for 30 days; every service answers /healthz and /readyz (D9)
interfaces: REST /v1/* JSON; errors {code, message, details}; OpenAPI served at /docs
Every table has paper_id; every request resolves its paper from the session or API key
Job envelope {type, paper_id, payload, idempotency_key}
Env: DATABASE_URL FILES_DRIVER FILES_ROOT S3_* ANTHROPIC_API_KEY APP_SECRET
done_when: docker compose up gives healthy api, worker, ops, postgres and proxy on one 4 vCPU / 16 GB Linux box
Seed creates a demo paper + owner; a viewer is refused on save
A failing job retries 3 times, then shows in the dead-letter list
A test proves paper A cannot read paper B's rows or files
Stop and start the whole stack: every row, file and queued job is still there

modules.name: CONNECTOR HUB
modules.purpose: Any website in. One Article out.
build: Connector interface: discover(cfg, since) lists refs; fetch(cfg, ref) returns a RawItem
Kinds in v1: push · rss · wordpress · rest · cxml · scrape (ghost, drupal, newsml arrive later as adapters)
normalize(raw, mapping) → Article; zod-validate; reject with reasons, never half-save
Upsert key (paper_id, source_id, external_id); content_hash decides whether it changed
Port parseCXML() from the prototype: copes with image tags nested mid-sentence, quote blocks, missing ids
Scheduler per source (cron), push endpoint with HMAC check, file-drop watcher
Mapping wizard + TEST endpoint: a dry run that returns 5 parsed articles and every error
interfaces: IN wire 1: RawItem (XML node · feed item · JSON · HTML)
OUT wire 2: Article (D1) · wire 3: asset jobs
POST /v1/ingest/articles · POST /v1/sources · POST /v1/sources/:id/test · POST /v1/sources/:id/sync
Internal events article.created · article.updated
done_when: BlinkCMS Punjabi sample → 2 pages, 9 stories + 1 advert, 7 image refs; ContentXML export re-parses identical
A stock WordPress site and a plain RSS feed ingest with mapping only, zero code
HTML door gets headline, body and lead image from 3 unseen news sites on wizard defaults
Re-sync with no changes writes nothing; an edited article bumps rev and flags the pages that use it

modules.name: ASSET PIPELINE
modules.purpose: Every picture ready for screen, print and cut-out.
modules.tech: sharp (libvips) · existing Card Maker cut-out model in the browser · Poppler for PDF artwork
build: Download originals (follow redirects, size cap, type sniff); store once per content hash
Derivatives: thumb 400 px and web 1600 px WebP; the print file is always the untouched original
Focal point: subject box from the Card Maker model in the browser (SEG.subject), sharp attention crop on the server; a tap overrides
Cut-out provider A, already built: Card Maker's in-browser model, SEG.cut(img) → canvas + mask → uploaded as asset kind cutout
Cut-out provider B: a server worker with the same output, for auto-plan and batch runs
Print check: needed px = frame width in inches × 150; warn in the editor, block nothing
PDF or EPS artwork named by feeds (feature-1.pdf) → rasterise at 300 dpi
interfaces: IN wire 3: {article_id, url} or an upload
OUT: Asset row + files; derivatives {thumb, web, cutout} · focal [x, y] · px [w, h]
POST /v1/assets · POST /v1/assets/:id/cutout · GET /v1/assets/:id
Wire 4: CutoutProvider.cut(image) → {png_alpha, subject_box} — one interface, two providers
done_when: 100 mixed JPG / PNG / WebP URLs ingest; duplicates are stored once
A cut-out shows in the editor with text wrapping its outline within 10 s
Low-res warning matches the prototype at Broadsheet and Tabloid
Provider down: the photo is still usable, the cut-out retries, the editor is told

modules.name: AI ASSIST
modules.tech: Claude API (model id from env) · JSON-only outputs · results cached by content hash
build: Tasks: shorten_headline(max_chars, n=3) · standfirst · caption · pull_quote · trim_to_fit(words_over) · classify_section
trim_to_fit returns paragraph / sentence indexes to cut — never rewritten text
pull_quote must be an exact substring of the body; checked in code
Output language = article language (Punjabi stays Punjabi); a mismatch is rejected
Every suggestion is stored with prompt hash, model, and who accepted or rejected it
interfaces: POST /v1/ai/suggest {task, article_id, constraints} → {suggestions[]}
Wire 7 → the editor's AI panel and the M4 fit loop, as proposals only
Queue ai; 30 s timeout; on failure there is no suggestion and the editor carries on
done_when: 3 headline options within max_chars for the English and the Punjabi sample
No saved page ever changes without an accept event in the audit log
Pull-quote substring test passes on 50 articles
API key missing → AI panel hidden, nothing else breaks

modules.name: LAYOUT ENGINE + TEMPLATES
modules.purpose: Turns a day's articles into pages that fit.
modules.tech: packages/layout: HTML + CSS grid shared by editor and worker · Playwright Chromium · self-hosted woff2 fonts
build: Template = page size + 8-column grid + slots[{id, span, cols, kind, words_min, words_max, image}] + CSS + fonts
Slot ids stay compatible with feed names: story_col_span-N-k · sidebar · feature-n · editorial · adverts-n
Port from the prototype: row packer (stretch the last story so no hole is left), fit meter, auto-fit text size
Auto-plan: section → page; pick a template variant by story count and lengths; fill slots by priority; honour layout_hint
Fit loop per page: render → measure fill % → body size within [min, max] pt → image ratio → ask M3 for a cut list → flag overflow
Snapshot: getBoundingClientRect of every frame → mm → LayoutSnapshot (D4)
Cut-out wrap: CSS shape-outside from the alpha image; the snapshot records wrap: alpha
Fonts per paper: licensed families uploaded as woff2; the same family names must be installed on the InDesign machine
Phase 2: story jumps (continued on page N), baseline grid, Indic hyphenation
interfaces: IN wire 5: Articles + template set + ad bookings
OUT wire 6: PageDoc (D3) · wire 8: LayoutSnapshot (D4)
POST /v1/editions · POST /v1/editions/:id/autoplan · POST /v1/pages/:id/fit
renderPage(pageDoc, template) → HTML: the same function in browser and worker
done_when: Punjabi sample plans to 2 pages; page 1 fits; page 2 reports its overflow honestly (too much copy)
The same PageDoc in editor and headless: screenshot difference under 0.5 %
15 English articles → 4 pages in under 60 s
Same inputs give the same plan on every run

modules.name: EDITION EDITOR
modules.purpose: Where the sub-editor works, phone to desktop.
modules.tech: React + TypeScript (Vite) around packages/layout · contenteditable · command-stack undo
build: Port the prototype tools 1:1 first: edit text, width, text columns, headline size, move across pages, photos, add story / page, page sizes
Load + autosave PageDoc (2 s debounce) with rev; a stale save shows both versions and never overwrites silently
Unsaved typing is also kept in the browser (IndexedDB). API down? The editor keeps working and saves itself when it returns
Page lock: one editor per page, live presence, 2 min heartbeat
Story tray: unplaced articles, tap or drag to place; a source updated badge with merge
Undo / redo for every tool action; version list with restore
AI panel (M3): accept or reject options; cut-out toggle on photos (M2)
Page status: draft → subbed → approved (locked) → exported
interfaces: GET /v1/editions/:id · PUT /v1/pages/:id {doc, rev} → 409 on a stale rev
POST /v1/pages/:id/approve · GET /v1/pages/:id/versions · POST /v1/pages/:id/restore
Uses M4 renderPage() and the fit meter in the browser; asks /fit for server truth before approve
Print copy lives in the PageDoc: editing a page never edits the website article
done_when: Every prototype action survives a reload
Two browsers on one page: the second is read-only and sees who holds the lock
Restore brings back the text, photos and layout of any earlier version
Usable at 390 px wide: toolbar reachable, zoom works, no lost taps
Stop the API mid-edit, keep typing, start it again: every word is saved

modules.name: IDML EXPORT
modules.purpose: Hands InDesign a page that is 80 % done.
modules.tech: packages/idml: JSZip + XML builders · IDML = a zip of XML (designmap, Spreads, Stories, Resources)
build: Skeleton: the client's own template saved as .idml (keeps their styles, masters, swatches, fonts); fallback is our minimal skeleton
Per page: Spread + Page; one TextFrame each for kicker / head / sub; one multi-column TextFrame per body (TextColumnCount, TextColumnGutter)
One Stories/Story_*.xml per frame; paragraph style names = feed names (Story-head, Story-body, Side-body …)
Photos: Rectangle + Image + Link LinkResourceURI="file:Links/100.jpg"; cut-outs get contour text wrap by alpha channel
Indic styles: Composer="HL Composer Optyca" (World-Ready Paragraph Composer); font family names identical to the CSS
mm → pt (× 2.8346); spread-origin maths per the IDML spec; zip with mimetype first and uncompressed
Overflow is exported as overset text, never cut, so the operator sees it
interfaces: IN wire 8: LayoutSnapshot + print originals from M2
OUT wire 9: {paper}_{date}.zip → one .idml with all pages + Links/
POST /v1/editions/:id/exports {format: "idml", pages?} → job → signed URL
Phase 2: IDML re-import (read back moved frames and edited text)
done_when: Opens in the client's InDesign with no repair or missing-plugin dialog
Frames within 0.5 mm of the browser layout; photos relink when Links/ sits beside the file
The operator's existing paragraph styles apply untouched; Punjabi and Telugu shape correctly
CI checks zip layout + well-formed XML on every export; one manual open per new template

modules.name: PDF + XML EXPORT
modules.purpose: Proofs, papers with no InDesign, and the way back to Typefi.
modules.tech: Playwright page.pdf() · qpdf · Ghostscript for CMYK / PDF-X (phase 2)
build: Screen PDF: render the edition HTML with @page = paper size, fonts embedded, RGB — the proof and the e-paper source
ContentXML: port toCXML(); slot names carry the current spans; round-trip test in CI
Press PDF (phase 2): Ghostscript → CMYK with a newspaper ICC profile, PDF/X output intent, images to 200 dpi, preflight report
Per-page and whole-edition files named {paper}_{date}_p{NN}
interfaces: IN wire 8: LayoutSnapshot + PageDoc
OUT wire 12: screen PDF + snapshot → M8
POST /v1/editions/:id/exports {format: "pdf_screen" | "pdf_press" | "cxml"}
GET /v1/exports/:id → {status, url, log}
done_when: PDF page box equals the chosen size to 0.1 mm; all fonts embedded; text selectable
ContentXML export of the sample re-parses to the same model (already true in the prototype)
Press PDF stays labelled experimental until one press trial is signed off

modules.name: E-PAPER PIPELINE
modules.purpose: Final PDF in. Tappable edition out.
modules.tech: Poppler (pdfinfo pdfseparate pdftoppm pdftotext -bbox-layout) · sharp · Tesseract OCR fallback · Postgres full-text
build: Accept a whole-edition PDF, single-page PDFs, or a LayoutSnapshot (the no-InDesign route). Store the upload first, process it second
Split → rasterise at 200 dpi → WebP 400 / 1600 / 3200 px wide; keep each page PDF for download
Text: words with boxes → lines → blocks. Text layer unreadable (legacy Indic fonts)? OCR the page image instead
Zones: headline candidates (largest type) → fuzzy-match the day's Articles → grow the region by body overlap → rect list + confidence
Prior: edition built here? Start from the snapshot frames and only verify
Replace page: reprocess that page only; version + 1, corrected = true; the old version is kept for rollback
Scheduler publishes at publish_at; cache purge; webhook out
interfaces: IN wire 11: final PDF · wire 12: screen PDF + snapshot
OUT wire 13: ep_pages (images, text) + ep_zones (D5)
POST /v1/epaper/editions (multipart) · PUT /v1/epaper/editions/:id/pages/:no · PATCH /v1/epaper/pages/:id/zones
POST /v1/epaper/editions/:id/publish {at} · POST /v1/epaper/editions/:id/rollback
done_when: A 24-page PDF is processed in under 2 min on the target box
At least 85 % of stories auto-zoned on an English edition; every miss is listed for manual fix
A legacy-font Punjabi PDF still gets zones through OCR or the snapshot prior
Page replace is live within 60 s; rollback restores the old image and zones

modules.name: READER
modules.tech: Static TypeScript app (Preact) · service worker · served from a CDN or the paper's own domain
build: Routes /{paper}/{date}/{page}; latest redirect; edition switcher; archive calendar
Page view: swipe, pinch zoom (swap to the 3200 px image), thumbnail strip
Zones overlay: tap → story sheet with the Article text and Read on site → Article.url
Search inside one edition and across the archive; hits highlight their zones
Share: crop the zone to an image card + link (Web Share, WhatsApp fallback)
Offline: last opened edition cached; page PDF download
interfaces: IN wire 13 through GET /v1/public/papers/:slug/editions?date= · /editions/:id/pages · /pages/:id/zones · /search?q=
Gate hook from M11 (paywall); event beacons to M11 (analytics)
Wire 14: back-links to the website
done_when: First page visible in under 2 s on 4G; installable as an app
A zone opens the right story on 20 of 20 sampled taps
Works at 360 px and 1440 px; Gurmukhi, Telugu and Latin render in the story sheet
The last edition reopens in airplane mode

modules.name: SITE KIT (OUT)
modules.purpose: Lets any website carry, trust and hear from the e-paper.
modules.tech: embed.js (about 5 kB) · signed webhooks · public read API · JWT verify · Caddy on-demand TLS
build: embed.js finds <div data-epaper>, mounts a responsive iframe, uses postMessage for height and deep links
Custom domain per paper by CNAME with automatic certificates
Webhooks: edition.published · edition.updated · page.replaced · export.ready; HMAC-SHA256 header; 5 retries with backoff
SSO: the site issues a short-lived JWT; the reader treats that visitor as a subscriber
SEO: story landing pages with canonical → site article; a sitemap per paper
interfaces: <script src="https://HOST/embed.js" data-paper="slug" data-edition="latest">
POST {site_hook_url} with X-Epaper-Signature; body {event, paper, edition, page?, url}
GET /v1/public/* with CORS and cache headers · GET /{paper}/sitemap.xml
done_when: One tag shows the latest edition inside a plain HTML page and inside a WordPress post
The sample receiver verifies the signature; a replayed delivery is rejected
An expired or forged JWT shows the paywall, never a crash

modules.name: REVENUE + ANALYTICS
modules.tech: Razorpay Subscriptions · events table → daily roll-ups
build: Paywall rules per paper: free pages N, free days, subscriber-only archive
Razorpay plans, checkout, webhook → subscriptions; grace period on failed renewals
Ad slots: between pages and banner; source = uploaded creative, booking feed, or ad-server tag
Events: page_view · zone_open · share · search · dwell; dashboard by page, story, day
interfaces: GET /v1/public/entitlement → {access, reason}
POST /v1/public/events (batched beacons)
POST /v1/webhooks/razorpay (signature verified)
Admin: /v1/papers/:id/paywall · /ads · /analytics
done_when: A test-mode payment unlocks the reader within 10 s; a cancelled plan locks at period end
An ad slot shows the booked creative on its dates only
Dashboard totals equal raw event counts for a sample day

modules.name: ADMIN CONSOLE
modules.purpose: Run many papers from one screen.
modules.tech: React (same shell as the editor) · role-gated routes · everything through /v1
build: Papers: name, language, script, page size, timezone, domain, theme
Sources: add / edit, mapping wizard, TEST, sync log, error inbox
Templates: grid + slot editor, font upload, client .idml skeleton upload
Users + roles; audit log viewer
E-paper desk: drop a PDF → progress → thumbnail grid → replace · hide · reorder · fix zones
Publish schedule (say 05:00), version list, one-tap rollback
A status light in the header: green, or a link straight to the ops desk (M13)
interfaces: Only the public /v1 API — no private back doors
Zone fixer writes PATCH /v1/epaper/pages/:id/zones with source: manual
Saving a template triggers a re-fit preview through M4
done_when: New paper to first auto-planned edition in under 15 min using only this console
A wrong zone is fixed in 3 taps and survives a later page replace when the story is unchanged
Every destructive action asks once and lands in the audit log

modules.name: OPS DESK + RECOVERY
modules.purpose: The owner fixes anything, at any hour, and loses nothing.
modules.tech: apps/ops: one small Node service with its own port, login and state file · Docker Engine API · WAL-G (Postgres, to the minute) · restic (files) · any S3 bucket off the box
build: Stands alone: own container, own login (password + TOTP, lock after 5 wrong tries), own state in ops/state.sqlite. It must answer when the API, the worker, Postgres and the proxy are all down
One row per service from ops/services.yml (D9): api · worker · postgres · proxy · reader · backups · disk · certificate, plus watch-only rows for the bucket, the Claude API and each source
Each row: a light (green · amber · red), since when, the last error in plain words, Restart, Logs

Fix buttons, every one safe to press twice: retry failed jobs · pause or resume a queue · re-sync a source · re-process an e-paper page · renew the certificate · free disk space (it lists what it will remove first)
Releases: every deploy is a tagged image set. Roll back to any of the last 5 in one tap; expand-only migrations keep that safe

Database: WAL shipped off the box every 60 s, a base backup every night, 30 days kept. Restore to a minute builds a second Postgres beside the live one, shows row counts side by side, then switches. The old one stays for 7 days
Files: written once, so nothing is ever overwritten. Copied off the box every 15 min with .env and the config; deletes are soft for 30 days. Restore one file, one edition, or everything
Every destructive button takes a snapshot first and asks for a typed confirmation. Every press lands in the ops log

Alerts to the owner's phone (Telegram or email) with a link to the fix: failed check · failed backup · disk over 80 % · certificate under 14 days. Plus one uptime monitor outside the box, because a dead box cannot report itself
A restore drill runs by itself every week into a scratch database; the desk shows backups verified with the date
scripts/restore.sh: on a fresh Linux box it needs only the recovery kit (bucket keys + backup password) to bring the whole system back
interfaces: Front door https://ops.HOST. Back door: the desk's own port :9443, for when the proxy is down
Ops API (D10): GET /ops/status · POST /ops/services/:name/restart · POST /ops/releases/:tag/rollback · POST /ops/db/restore
Reads /healthz and /readyz of every service (D9). A new service later is one more entry in ops/services.yml, no desk code
Promise: crash, restart, bad release or power cut = nothing saved is lost. Dead disk = at most about 1 min of database writes and 15 min of files
Time back: one service 1 min · a bad release 2 min · the whole box on new hardware 60 min
Zero loss even on a dead disk comes later: a second server with a synchronous replica
done_when: Stop each container in turn: its light is red within 30 s and one tap brings it back
Drop a table on purpose, then restore to 5 minutes earlier: every row is back, and the newer rows are still in the old copy
Ship a broken release: rolled back from the desk in under 2 min
Fill the disk to 95 %: the desk frees space; no original and no backup is touched
restore.sh on an empty VM: the latest edition opens within 60 min
With api, worker and Postgres all stopped, the desk still loads and can start them
The owner fixes a planted fault alone, from a phone, without a terminal

wires.name: RawItem
wires.what: Whatever the source gives: XML node, feed item, JSON, HTML. Pulled on schedule, pushed by webhook, or dropped as a file.

wires.name: Article · D1
wires.what: Canonical JSON. Upsert on paper + source + external id; the content hash decides whether it changed.

wires.name: Asset
wires.what: Image URLs become asset jobs. Originals and derivatives land in the store.

wires.name: Cut-out
wires.what: Photo in → PNG with alpha + subject box out. Browser model first, server worker for batches.

wires.name: Plan input
wires.what: The day's Articles, the paper's template set, the booked ad slots.

wires.name: PageDoc · D3
wires.what: One JSON per page. The planner writes it; the editor loads and saves it with a revision check.

wires.name: Suggestion
wires.what: Options from AI, shown in the editor. Applied only on accept.

wires.name: Layout Snapshot · D4
wires.what: Every frame of every approved page in mm, with text, style and asset. The only geometry exporters get.

wires.name: IDML package
wires.what: One zip: the .idml plus a Links/ folder of print originals. The operator downloads it.

wires.name: PDF/X
wires.what: Made by the client's operator on the client's licence. We never touch press output.

wires.name: Final PDF
wires.what: Uploaded whole, or one page at a time for corrections.

wires.name: Screen PDF + zones
wires.what: For papers that skip InDesign: our PDF and our snapshot go straight to the pipeline.

wires.name: Edition · D5
wires.what: Page images at 400 / 1600 / 3200 px, zones JSON, text index.

wires.name: Site loop
wires.what: A tap opens Article.url on the site. embed.js mounts the reader in the site. Webhooks announce editions.

wire_routes.6: M0 <-> M5 (M4 and M5 share one renderer)
wire_routes.ops: M13 watches every service, ships Postgres + files to the off-box bucket, and restores from it

runs.run: RUN 1 A DAILY EDITION, WITH INDESIGN
steps: wire 1: The site publishes or updates a story
wire 2 · 3: M1 maps it to an Article; M2 fetches the photos
wire 5: M4 auto-plans the pages
wire 6 · 7: The desk edits and approves in M5
wire 8 · 9: M6 exports the IDML package
wire 10: The operator polishes and sends PDF/X to press
wire 11: The same final PDF is uploaded to us
wire 13: M8 builds the e-paper; it publishes at the set hour
wire 14: Readers tap through to the site
wire 1 – 7: Same as run 1, up to page approval
wire 8: M7 renders the screen PDF from the approved pages
wire 12: PDF + snapshot go straight to M8; zones come from the snapshot, no guessing
wire 13: Published at the set hour; readers open it
A mistake is spotted on page 5
The operator fixes it in InDesign and exports that one page
wire 11: Admin console: replace page 5
M8 reprocesses only that page: version + 1, marked corrected
wire 14: Webhook page.replaced fires; readers see it on refresh
Wrong fix? Roll back in one tap
A health check fails. The owner's phone gets an alert with a link
M13: The ops desk shows which service is red, since when, and its last error in plain words
M13: One tap: restart it, retry the failed jobs, or roll back the release
M13: Data damaged? Restore to the minute before, beside the live database, compare, then switch
M5: Meanwhile the editors' typing waits in the browser and saves itself when the API returns
M13: All lights green. Every press is in the ops log

doors_in.use_when: Best door. The site or a CMS plugin POSTs each publish and update to /v1/ingest/articles.
doors_in.site_gives: One HTTP call. We issue the API key and HMAC secret.

doors_in.use_when: The site already publishes RSS, Atom, JSON Feed or a news sitemap.
WordPress REST (/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?_embed), Ghost, Drupal JSON:API, Strapi, or any REST / GraphQL endpoint.
doors_in.site_gives: Base URL. A read token if the API is private.

doors_in.use_when: The CMS exports files: Typefi ContentXML (BlinkCMS), NewsML-G2, NITF, DOCX.
doors_in.site_gives: Upload, SFTP or a bucket folder.

doors_in.use_when: No feed and no API. We read article pages with CSS selectors, else JSON-LD NewsArticle + OpenGraph + Readability.
doors_in.site_gives: Section URLs. Only sites the paper owns or has rights to. robots.txt is honoured.

mapping.principle: Each source row stores mapping_json: canonical field ← path + transforms. JSONPath for JSON, XPath for XML, CSS selectors for HTML, jsonld: for schema.org data.
wizard_order: RSS / Atom autodiscovery link → feed door
mapping.test: Then TEST shows 5 parsed articles and every validation error before anything is saved.
mapping.layout_hints: Layout hints ride along: ContentXML slot names such as story_col_span-3-1, sidebar, feature-1 become layout_hint. Sources without hints are auto-placed by M4.

doors_out.what: One script tag or iframe shows the reader inside any page. Or a CNAME: epaper.yoursite.com.
Every tap zone carries Article.url. Readers land on the site's own article page; canonical tags point home.
edition.published edition.updated page.replaced export.ready — HMAC signed, retried with backoff.
Editions, pages, zones and search as JSON with CORS. Enough to build a custom front end.
The site signs a short-lived JWT; the reader treats that visitor as a subscriber.

Pick templates: or upload the client .idml

D9_HEALTH_AND_SERVICE_LIST.about: how the desk knows a service
D9_HEALTH_AND_SERVICE_LIST.example:
// every service we run answers these two
GET /healthz   → 200 {"ok": true}                      // the process is alive
GET /readyz    → 200 {"ok": true,  "checks": {"db": "ok", "files": "ok"}}
               → 503 {"ok": false, "checks": {"db": "timeout after 5 s"}}

// ops/services.yml: one entry = one row on the desk
- name: worker
  container: epaper-worker
  ready: http://worker:3001/readyz
  needs: [postgres, files]             # red here? fix those first
  fixes: [restart, logs, retry_jobs]
- name: postgres
  container: epaper-postgres
  ready: pg_isready
  fixes: [restart, logs, restore_to_minute]
- name: backups
  ready: wal_age_s < 180 and files_age_min < 30
  fixes: [run_now, verify_now]
- name: claude-api                     # outside link: watch only
  ready: https://api.anthropic.com
  fixes: []

# a new service later = one more entry here, no desk code

contract_rules: Schemas live in packages/core as zod. TypeScript types are inferred from them, never written twice.
Add fields freely. Never rename or re-type one: a breaking change is a new contract version.
Fixtures are the tests' truth: fixtures/blinkcms-poc.cxml · fixtures/english-15.json · fixtures/edition-24p.pdf.
Ids are prefixed strings (pap_ src_ art_ ast_ ed_ it_ z_) so logs read themselves.
Times are ISO 8601 with offset. Geometry is mm on pages and 0–1 fractions on e-paper images.

notes: pages.doc (a PageDoc) is the truth for a page. page_articles is only an index answering: where is this article used?
ep_zones.article_id may be null: an advert or an unmatched story still gets a zone, fixed by hand later.
assets.parent_id links a cut-out to its photo. The print file is always the untouched original.
The job queue is tables too (pgboss schema), so one database backup covers rows and queued work. The ops desk keeps its own small state outside Postgres, on purpose.

build_order.done_rule: A module is finished only when its DONE WHEN list passes — as automated tests wherever a test can check it.

clock_72h.starts: when the owner writes 'build' in the build session
clock_72h.note: The clock starts when the owner writes build in the build session. STATUS.md records the start, the deadline and one entry every hour; the ops desk shows it. A missing input never stops the build: it is stubbed, listed under WAITING ON OWNER, and is not counted as a miss.
clock_72h.pause_risk: A usage cap or a closed session can pause the agent. The next session reads STATUS.md and carries on. Paused hours still count, so the cut order protects the deadline.
